title: MenuButton
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box holding a MonarchButton (androidx.compose.material3.Button) and MonarchMenu with MonarchMenuItem
summary: A button that opens a menu of actions: a MonarchButton with a trailing chevron and a MonarchMenu, placed together in a Box. Monarch ships no type for it.
whenToUse: For a short list of actions that belong to one object or screen, such as Rename, Duplicate and Delete, when there is no single main action.
whenNotToUse: When one action is the usual choice, use MonarchSplitButton. For choosing a value in a form use ExposedDropdownMenuBox. For a row's overflow menu with an icon only, use a MonarchIconButton with a content description as the trigger.
api: Box { MonarchButton(text: String, onClick = { expanded = true }, trailingIcon = { MonarchIcon(…, contentDescription = null) }); MonarchMenu(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit) { MonarchMenuItem(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, …) } }

options.name: expanded
options.description: Whether the menu is open; kept by the app with rememberSaveable.

options.name: variant
options.description: The trigger's weight: Primary, Secondary, Ghost or Danger.

options.name: size
options.description: The trigger's height: Sm, Md or Lg; the touch target is 48dp at every size.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: The chevron, a MonarchIcon with a null content description. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: enabled
options.description: On the MonarchButton: a disabled trigger does not open the menu.

states.name: closed
states.description: The trigger looks like any MonarchButton of its variant, with the chevron after the label.

states.name: open
states.description: The menu appears under the trigger (above when there is no room) and takes focus; the trigger's state is "Expanded".

states.name: disabled
states.description: The trigger uses the disabled colors and cannot open the menu.

appearance: The trigger follows the MonarchButton variant colors; the menu is the MonarchMenu on the raised background role with the default text role, and a danger item uses the strong danger role through destructive = true. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web MenuButton is a Radix MonarchMenu trigger with an items shorthand, controlled open state, alignment, side and a chevron that turns while open. On Android the MonarchMenu places the menu and handles back and outside taps, so the recipe is a MonarchButton and a MonarchMenu in one Box; the chevron does not turn. The items shorthand is a list of MonarchMenuItems; links open from the item's onClick. iOS covers it with the system Menu and the Monarch button style.
accessibility: The trigger is a Button with its label; the recipe adds the stateDescription "Expanded" or "Collapsed" and the expand and collapse actions so TalkBack says what the button does.
The chevron has a null content description; an icon-only trigger needs a content description such as "More actions".
Menu items are 48dp tall and the menu takes focus when it opens (system behavior).
A danger item says what it does ("Delete"); its color is not the only signal.
edgeCases: Close the menu (expanded = false) in each item's onClick; it does not close by itself.
A long label wraps inside the trigger rather than widening it past the screen.
There is no loading state on the trigger; disable it while the actions are unavailable.

parityExceptions.reason: The danger tone is MonarchMenuItem destructive = true.
parityExceptions.convention: Material 3 menus: a destructive item is marked by its colour role
